newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sees higher tobacco output this year.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sees higher tobacco output this year.

text.p: Bulgaria's tobacco output is expected to rise this year, after suffering a record low output in 1995, private tobacco growers said on Wednesday .

"Bulgaria expects to produce some 38,000 tonnes of tobacco in 1996, which is 13,000 tonnes up on the tobacco produced in 1995 when output hit a record low," Georgi Petrov, chairman of the Tobacco Producers' Union, told a news conference.

He said that last year was "nightmarish" for Bulgaria's tobacco industry due to unfavourable weather conditions and low purchase prices, which forced the poverty-stricken population in tobacco growing areas to launch more profitable businesses.
Bulgaria's tobacco exports are aimed mainly to western companies.

Six years ago, when tobacco output reached some 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes annually, the Balkan country exported some 40,000 tonnes of tobacco to the former Soviet Union and only 10,000 to western buyers.
Tobacco growing is export-oriented with long traditions in Bulgaria where some 800,000 people are involved, which is nearly 10 percent of the country's population, mainly of ethnic Turks.
